item.name: Category Assignments
item.description: STG-404 admin CRUD for category routing rules: one rule per department and service category. Requires a Grievance Admin or System Manager bearer token.

request.description: List rules. Optional query: service_category, department, active, page, page_size. Newest first. The page info (page, page_size, total_count, total_pages, has_next, has_prev) is in data.pagination. Unknown query parameters return 400.

Create the rule for one department and service category: a category-only routing desk plus the category SLA row. Required: service_category, department, l1_officer, sla_days. One rule per department and category, inactive ones included. sla_days and auto_escalate belong to the category, so departments serving the same category share them.
Fetch one rule by its Grievance RBAC Assignment id, for example GR-RBAC-00001.
Partial update. Service category cannot be changed. Send l2_officer null to clear it. Changing sla_days or auto_escalate changes the category SLA row for every department serving it.
Deactivate the rule: its routing desk is marked inactive and kept for audit. The category SLA row is not changed. Same as PATCH with active false; repeating the call changes nothing.

item.name: SLA Settings
item.description: STG-412 admin API for the SLA tab: the global SLA policy and the per-category SLA windows. Per-category sla_days and auto_escalate are the same values as Category Assignments. Writes need a Grievance Admin or System Manager bearer token.

request.description: Installation-wide policy: max_deferral_days, auto_escalation_threshold (percent) and requires_supervisor_approval (true: a senior officer decides a deferral; false: the assigned officer may approve it).
Send any of the three fields; omitted fields stay as they are.

Per-category SLA window, auto-escalate and notify-on-breach flags, with the departments serving each category. Optional query: service_category, department, page, page_size. Saves the first row's id as sla_configuration.
Send any of sla_days, auto_escalate and notify_on_breach. The values are shared with Category Assignments for the same category. Run List category SLA settings first to set sla_configuration.

item.name: Service Categories & Grievance Types
item.description: STG-406 admin CRUD for the service categories and grievance types the submission wizard, category assignments and response templates share. Requires a Grievance Admin or System Manager bearer token for writes; Grievance Review Officer may read. Records are retired, never deleted.

request.description: List categories in display order, active and inactive. Optional query: is_active, search (name or code), page, page_size. Each record counts the active types, assignments and templates that refer to it. Unknown query parameters return 400. Grievance Review Officer may call this.

Create a category. Required: category_name, code. The code is the 3-character ticket segment, in the ticket alphabet (no I, L, O or U), and unique. sort_order is optional and defaults to the end of the list; is_active defaults to true. is_default (default false) true makes this the category unclassified cases fall to and clears the flag on the previous default; it needs is_active true. Duplicate name or code returns 409.
One category, by name or ticket code. 404 when unknown.

Partial update of category_name, code, sort_order, is_active or is_default. Renaming keeps every grievance, type, routing rule, SLA row and template linked and runs in the background: the response keeps the old category_name and shows renaming_to until the job is done, then the category answers to the new name. The code cannot change once tickets exist (code_locked). Setting is_active false also deactivates its types, and is refused for the default category. is_default true makes this the default (the previous default loses the flag); false is refused because exactly one category must be the default.

Make this the default category: the one cases with no category (an IVR call or email that named none, a draft saved without a choice) are filed under. The previous default loses the flag, and the new default gets an active catch-all Other type if it has none. The category must be active. Send the same request for another category to move the default; is_default false is refused.

Retire the category and its types (refused for the default category: make another the default first). Nothing is deleted: grievances keep them and the submission dropdowns stop offering them. Routing rules and templates already set up on the category stay active for open cases. Same as PATCH with is_active false; repeating the call changes nothing.

List types by category and name, active and inactive. Optional query: service_category (name or code), is_active, search (text in the type name), page, page_size. Unknown query parameters return 400. Grievance Review Officer may call this.

Create a type under an active category. Required: service_category (name or code), type_name. The name is unique within the category (the same name under another category is allowed). Duplicate returns 409.
One type, by grievance_type_id. 404 when unknown.

Partial update of type_name or is_active. The service category cannot change. A type cannot be reactivated while its category is inactive, and the catch-all Other type of the default category cannot be deactivated.
Retire the type. Grievances keep it and the submission dropdowns stop offering it. Same as PATCH with is_active false; repeating the call changes nothing.

item.name: Officers
item.description: STG-430 admin CRUD for L1 (Nodal) and L2 (Senior Nodal) officers, extended by STG-443 to Admin and Reviewer accounts through the same resource: role is Officer (the default), Admin or Reviewer. An officer is a User placed on category desks, so the id is the account's email and every service category must already have a category assignment for the department. An Admin or Reviewer is a plain User with that role and no desk, so it takes no part in routing, escalation or officer statistics. An account holds one grievance role. Requires a Grievance Admin bearer token; resetting an Admin's password needs a System Manager or Administrator. Accounts are deactivated by updating status, not deleted. Performance metrics come from the statistics API.

request.description: Filter by role (Officer by default, or Admin or Reviewer), level (L1/L2), department, status, service_category, region (exact area), or search text q. level, department, service_category and region are officer filters: they return 400 with role=Admin or Reviewer, as does status On Leave. Paginated with page and page_size; the pagination block is at the top level of the response. Admin and Reviewer accounts never appear in the Officer list.

Create a Senior Nodal (L2) officer. The login is created when the email is new. temporary_password is required: the officer signs in with it only to replace it through POST /api/v1/auth/password/initial. An email that already has a login keeps its own password.
Create a Nodal (L1) officer. reports_to is an L2 officer id (their email) and is only valid for an L1. temporary_password is required and is applied to a new login only.

Reissue a temporary password to an officer, admin or reviewer, for example after a forgotten password. Its sessions end at once and the holder must replace the password through POST /api/v1/auth/password/initial before signing in. A Grievance Admin can reset Officers and Reviewers; an Admin account can be reset only by a System Manager or Administrator. Nobody resets their own password here, and System Manager and Administrator accounts are never reset here.

Fetch one account by email, of any role. An officer comes with the desks (RBAC assignments) they sit on; an Admin or Reviewer has empty level, department, region, reports_to, service_categories and assignments.
Move an officer between L1 and L2. The move clears their supervisor, and an L2 with L1 officers reporting to them cannot change level.
Partial update. service_categories replaces the whole list and re-seats the officer on those desks. Send phone, region or reports_to as null to clear them. email is rejected.
Deactivation is a status update: Active, On Leave or Inactive. On Leave skips auto-routing; Inactive also retires the officer's desk rows.

Active, On Leave, Inactive and total counts for the officers tabs, with the same filters as the list but no status. Each person is counted once, by the most available of their desk rows. The UI shows these in place of its hardcoded counts.
Counts of Admin accounts. Admin and Reviewer have no On Leave, so on_leave is 0. Needs an admin role: a Review Officer is refused with 403.
Admin accounts, by name. status, q, page and page_size apply as for officers.
Reviewer (Grievance Review Officer) accounts, by name.

Create a Grievance Admin. Only full_name, email, phone and temporary_password are required; designation is optional. level, department, service_categories, reports_to and region are refused. The login is created when the email is new, with this role alone. A login that holds a different grievance role is refused.
Create a Grievance Review Officer (read-only). Same fields and rules as Create admin.
level, department, service_categories, reports_to and region are not accepted for an Admin or Reviewer. The response is 400 VALIDATION_ERROR and details names each field.
One Admin or Reviewer by email. Needs an admin role.
An Admin or Reviewer takes only full_name, phone, designation and status. Anything else, including role and email, returns 400.

status Inactive disables the login and ends its sessions and refresh tokens, so it cannot sign in. You cannot deactivate your own account, and the last active Grievance Admin cannot be deactivated. On Leave returns 400.
status Active enables the login again. The password is unchanged.
A Grievance Admin can reset a Reviewer. An Admin's password can be reset only by a System Manager or Administrator; another Grievance Admin gets 403 PERMISSION_DENIED.

item.name: Notification Templates
item.description: Grievance notification templates and routing rules. Fetch active and inactive notification templates with event, channel, and recipient filtering. Requires a Grievance Officer, Grievance Admin, or System Manager bearer token.

request.description: List grievance notification templates. Returns both active and inactive by default. Optional filters: event, channel, recipient_type, role_level, enabled (true/false), page, page_size.
Returns available notification channels, flat recipient targets, active role levels, and allowed template placeholders.
Get available notification template placeholders with descriptions and examples.
Fetch a single grievance notification template by its document name / ID.
Partially update a notification template (enabled, subject, body, recipient_type, role_level). Requires Grievance Admin or System Manager.

item.name: Review Officer (read-only)
item.description: STG-434. The Grievance Review Officer reads grievances, officer statistics, departments, category assignments and Nodal and Senior Nodal Officers, and changes nothing. Sign in with 3. Login using a user that holds the Grievance Review Officer role. R requests return 200. W requests return 403 PERMISSION_DENIED: the role is refused on every create, edit, delete, assign and resolve call. STG-443: it reads officer status counts, but not Admin or Reviewer accounts, and cannot create, update or reset any account.
